title: Replace-import deletes the whole library before the file is parsed or validated
root_cause: doImport('replace') awaits chrome.storage.local.remove(['prompts_storage','prompts']) at line 1783 and only then calls PromptStorage.importPrompts(file), which throws on JSON.parse errors or 'Invalid JSON format' (promptStorage.js:476-501). There is no rollback. The removal also fires the auto-backup storage listener, which 2s later writes the now-empty library over the user's backup file.
suggested_fix: Parse and validate the file (or stage the import result) BEFORE removing existing data; or snapshot the current store and restore it in the catch block. Prefer a single atomic replace inside promptStorage.js.
failure_scenario: User picks a truncated/corrupt export.json, clicks Import (Replace), confirms. Storage is wiped, importPrompts throws, toast says 'Import failed' — all prompts are gone, and with auto-backup enabled the backup file is overwritten with an empty library 2 seconds later.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). npm test → 9/9 pass. doImport now reads+JSON.parses+validates shape BEFORE chrome.storage.local.remove, and snapshots the store for rollback if the post-wipe import throws. app.js UI flow verified by inspection (not unit-testable without a full DOM/module harness). Also resolves #71.

title: Unsaved editor changes are silently lost — dirty flag is tracked but never read
root_cause: renderEditor maintains `dirty` (set at 647/659/852, cleared at 745) but no code ever reads it (ESLint confirms: 'dirty' is assigned a value but never used). There is no beforeunload handler anywhere in app.js and handleRoute/navigate (85-128) never check for unsaved state before replacing the view. Title/tag/language edits don't even set the flag.
suggested_fix: Consume the dirty flag: intercept hashchange/navigation and window.beforeunload while dirty, prompting to save/discard; also mark dirty on titleInput/tag/langSel changes.
failure_scenario: User types a long new prompt in #/editor (never saved), then clicks 'Library' or a nav link. The view is replaced with no warning and the draft is unrecoverable — no version was ever stored.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). The pre-existing "'dirty' is assigned a value but never used" warning is now gone (dirty is read by the router guard). Added beforeunload + guarded hashchange (confirm/revert) and dirty-marking on title/category/language/tag edits. Verified by inspection + lint.

title: withLock serializes only within one JS context; app tab, service worker, and content scripts hold independent locks on the same store
root_cause: _writeChain is a module-level variable, so every context that imports promptStorage.js gets its own lock. The service worker imports it directly (service-worker.js:2), app.js imports it directly, and content scripts dynamically import the web-accessible copy (PromptStorageManager._ps). All three perform read->modify->write on the single prompts_storage key with no cross-context coordination. The comment claiming this fixes 'floating panel + app tab racing' is incorrect because the panel runs in a third module instance. chrome.storage.local has no transactions.
suggested_fix: Serialize mutations across contexts: route all writes through one owner (e.g. the service worker) via messaging, or implement a chrome.storage-based advisory lock / single-writer queue.
failure_scenario: App tab open while the floating panel is used on chatgpt.com: panel bumpUseCount/savePrompt reads the store at the same moment app.js updatePrompt reads it; both write back their own snapshot — one edit, new prompt, or use-count is silently clobbered (last-writer-wins whole-store overwrite).
verification_notes: Architectural: a true fix routes ALL prompts_storage writes through a single owner (service worker) or a chrome.storage advisory lock. chrome.storage.local has no atomic compare-and-swap, so a safe minimal cross-context lock is not feasible without refactoring every caller in app.js/service-worker.js/content scripts — out of scope for minimal edits and high regression risk. Partially mitigated by #6 (transact) and locked mutations (#36). Recommend a dedicated single-writer follow-up.

title: pickBackupFile ignores the user's chosen save-as location and always records the constant Downloads path
root_cause: After the saveAs:true download completes, the code stores downloadPath: BACKUP_PATH ('promptforge/promptforge-backup.json') and returns filePath: BACKUP_PATH, never reading the actual item.filename the user picked. writeBackup (line 143) then writes to settings.downloadPath || BACKUP_PATH, i.e. always the default Downloads subfolder, contradicting the file header strategy ('Subsequent auto-backups overwrite that same path'). Note chrome.downloads can only write under the Downloads directory, so an arbitrary iCloud/Dropbox location cannot be honored by this API at all.
suggested_fix: Read the completed download item's filename and persist that as downloadPath (and return it), or drop saveAs and use a fixed known path; document the Downloads-only limitation of chrome.downloads.
failure_scenario: User clicks 'Choose Backup Location' and saves to iCloud Drive/promptforge-backup.json for cross-machine sync. The first file lands in iCloud, but every later auto-backup writes to Downloads/promptforge/promptforge-backup.json; the iCloud copy stays stale forever and the second machine merges outdated data.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). npm test → 9/9 pass. pickBackupFile now uses saveAs:false with the fixed Downloads/promptforge path (chrome.downloads cannot write outside Downloads), so recurring writeBackup overwrites the same advertised file; header comment + app.js button label updated to match. Verified by inspection.

title: Shadow snapshot only saved when the file is written; stale shadow resurrects deleted prompts
root_cause: saveShadow (line 357, duplicated at 413-428 for the native transport) runs only inside `if (result.remoteChanged || !remote)`. When a cycle only pulls remote edits into local storage (localChanged=true, remoteChanged=false), local becomes equal to remote but the shadow keeps the OLD digests. For a prompt the user then deletes locally, mergeAll hits the `!L && R, S!==undefined && rChanged` branch (lines 225-228, 'deleted locally, edited remotely -> remote edit wins') and re-imports it.
suggested_fix: Always call saveShadow(result.prompts, result.folders, result.tombstones) after a successful merge (both transports), regardless of whether the file was written; the merged state is what both sides now agree on.
failure_scenario: Device B edits prompt X; device A syncs and pulls the edit (remoteChanged=false, so shadow not updated). User on A deletes X. On A's next cycle the stale shadow makes R look 'edited remotely', so X is restored locally and no tombstone is ever created — the deletion is silently undone on every cycle.
verification_notes: npm test → 9/9 pass. tests/syncEngine.test.js: pull-only cycle + refreshed shadow → local delete becomes a tombstone (regression); stale-shadow case documents the pre-fix resurrection. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). saveShadow moved outside the write-only branch in both transports.

title: Sync cycle's read-merge-write clobbers local edits made during the cycle
root_cause: The cycle snapshots the library via getPrompts()/getFolders() (lines 325-327; native: 392-395) and later bulk-replaces it with setPrompts(result.prompts) (line 338; native: 407). promptStorage's withLock (promptStorage.js:176-180) serializes individual writes but cannot protect the engine's multi-second read->merge->write span, which includes FS reads of iCloud-evicted files and, in the native path, several host process spawns/RPCs. Any savePrompt/updatePrompt/deletePrompt that commits in that window is overwritten by the stale snapshot.
suggested_fix: Re-read the library inside the same lock as the final write and re-merge (or apply per-prompt deltas instead of a bulk replace), or add a storage generation counter and abort/retry the cycle if prompts_storage changed since the snapshot.
failure_scenario: Native cycle starts (ping + get-folder + read RPCs take ~1-3s). While it is in flight the user saves a new prompt or edits one in the app tab. setPrompts(result.prompts) then writes the pre-edit snapshot — the user's save/edit is permanently lost (and never reaches the sync file).
verification_notes: npm test → 9/9 pass. tests/promptStorage.test.js: transact re-reads fresh state inside withLock and preserves an edit committed after the snapshot; null skips write. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). Added promptStorage.transact; both sync transports re-merge against fresh local state under the lock instead of bulk setPrompts(snapshot).

title: OpenRouter input[type=text] is never injected (only contenteditable/textarea handled)
root_cause: insertPrompt branches only on inputBox.contentEditable==='true' (line 127) and tagName==='textarea' (line 338); everything else hits the else at 352-355 which logs 'Unknown input box type' and returns without inserting. llm_providers.json:99 defines OpenRouter's element_selector as "input[type='text'][placeholder='Start a message...']", whose tagName is 'input', so it always falls into the dead else branch.
suggested_fix: Add an explicit branch for HTMLInputElement (set .value via the native prototype setter + dispatch input/change), or generalise the value-setting path to any element with a writable 'value' property.
failure_scenario: User on openrouter.ai selects a prompt -> getInputBox returns the text <input> -> insertPrompt logs 'Unknown input box type' and returns -> nothing is inserted and the panel does not even hide; injection is broken for the whole OpenRouter provider.

title: React-controlled textareas set .value directly, so onChange never fires
root_cause: The textarea path assigns inputBox.value = ... (lines 344/346) then dispatches a synthetic 'input' event. React installs a value tracker on controlled inputs; a plain .value assignment goes through React's own setter and updates the tracker, so the subsequent input event is deduped and React state is never updated. The native HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype value setter must be used to bypass the tracker. DeepSeek (textarea[placeholder='Message DeepSeek']), Poe (GrowingTextArea), GitHub Copilot, LMArena and Qwen are React-controlled textareas; exact per-site impact depends on each site's framework wiring.
suggested_fix: Use Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype,'value').set.call(inputBox, newValue) before dispatching the bubbling input event (the standard React-compatible injection technique).
failure_scenario: On chat.deepseek.com the user inserts a prompt: text appears in the box, but React state stays empty; pressing Send submits an empty message (or the box reverts on the next render), so injection silently fails on React-controlled providers.
verification_notes: npm test → 9/9 pass. tests/inputBoxHandler.test.js "#8 native setter bypasses React-style tracker" passes (native prototype value set, tracker untouched, input event fired). npm run bundle → exit 0. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50).

title: 15-second poll timeout revokes the blob URL while the save-as dialog may still be open
root_cause: The completion poll runs at most 30 attempts x 500ms = 15s. On timeout it clearInterval, URL.revokeObjectURL(url), and resolves enabled:false. With saveAs:true the download only begins writing after the user confirms the dialog, so revoking the blob URL before confirmation invalidates the source.
suggested_fix: Do not impose a short fixed timeout on a user-driven save-as dialog; wait for the download's terminal state (complete/interrupted/cancelled) via chrome.downloads.onChanged, and only revoke the URL after a terminal state.
failure_scenario: User opens the save-as dialog and takes 20s to navigate to a folder. At 15s the code revokes the blob and reports failure; when the user finally confirms, the download is interrupted (blob gone) and no backup file is created, yet the UI offered no error.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection (app.js/DOM or chrome.* API flow not unit-testable without a full harness). pickBackupFile now waits for the download terminal state via waitForDownload (onChanged) with a 120s safety net that does NOT revoke the blob prematurely.

title: writeBackup never verifies the download reached 'complete'; failed backups are silent
root_cause: chrome.downloads.download's callback fires when the download starts, not when it finishes. The code only logs chrome.runtime.lastError (null on a successful start) and revokes the URL after 1s; it never checks item.state, so an interrupted overwrite produces no user-visible error. The 1s revoke can also invalidate the blob mid-download for large libraries on slow disks.
suggested_fix: Track the download id to a terminal state (onChanged or search) and surface/log a failure when state is 'interrupted'; consider retrying. Only treat the backup as successful on state==='complete', and revoke the URL only then.
failure_scenario: Dropbox/antivirus holds a lock on promptforge-backup.json during sync; the overwrite download is interrupted after starting. lastError is null, nothing is logged or shown, and the user keeps relying on a backup file that is silently stale.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection (app.js/DOM or chrome.* API flow not unit-testable without a full harness). writeBackup awaits waitForDownload, logs interrupted/cancelled failures, and revokes the blob only on a terminal state (no 1s mid-flight revoke).

title: Streaming generator ignores mid-stream Ollama error objects, yielding silent truncation
root_cause: ollamaStreamGenerator only yields data.message.content and returns on data.done; a line like {"error":"..."} (model runner crash, OOM, context overflow) has neither field, so it is skipped and the stream ends normally. The service worker then posts {done:true} and the consumer treats partial/empty output as success.
suggested_fix: Detect data.error in the stream loop and throw an Error so the caller surfaces a failure instead of saving truncated output.
failure_scenario: Ollama emits {"error":"model runner has unexpectedly stopped"} partway through an Improve stream. The generator skips it, the panel receives done:true with a half-rewritten prompt, and that truncated text is saved as a new version with no error shown.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection (app.js/DOM or chrome.* API flow not unit-testable without a full harness). ollamaStreamGenerator throws on data.error (re-throws non-SyntaxError from the parse catch) so truncated output is surfaced, not saved as success.

title: Provider list caches an empty array permanently after a single transient fetch failure
root_cause: On any fetch/parse error _providers is set to [] and cached; _loadProviders returns the cached value forever after ([] is truthy, so the `if (_providers)` guard at line 8 short-circuits). getProviders then yields no providers for the rest of the service-worker lifetime, so tab-update injection and Send-to-Tab matching stop entirely. inputBoxHandler.js:7-23 deliberately does NOT cache failures — this module should match.
suggested_fix: Do not cache the failure case (leave _providers null so the next call retries), or cache with a short TTL / retry-on-empty.
failure_scenario: llm_providers.json fetch fails once at startup (transient I/O). _providers=[] is cached; for the whole browser session chrome.tabs.onUpdated finds no matching provider and the panel never injects on any LLM site until the browser is restarted.

title: Hand-rolled match-pattern regex over-matches because the scheme wildcard becomes an unanchored '.*' prefix
root_cause: Converting '*://chatgpt.com/*' yields /^.*://chatgpt\.com/.*/. The leading '.*' can absorb an entire preceding URL, so any tab whose URL merely contains '://chatgpt.com/' (e.g. in a query string) tests true. chrome.tabs.query elsewhere uses correct match-pattern semantics; only this regex is wrong. Actual injection is backstopped by host permissions, but the extension declares optional <all_urls>.
suggested_fix: Match the host explicitly (parse tab.url with new URL() and compare hostname/path against the provider pattern) or anchor the scheme to https?:// and the host to a boundary, rather than '.*://'.
failure_scenario: With a broad host grant, a tab at https://evil.com/?next=https://chatgpt.com/ matches the ChatGPT regex and the service worker injects content.bundle.js into evil.com, mounting the panel on a non-provider page.
verification_notes: npm test → 19/19 pass. tests/urlMatch.test.js (5 tests): provider host matches; evil.com/?next=chatgpt rejected; path-scoped + subdomain wildcard semantics. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings). SW onUpdated uses urlMatchesPattern.

title: Fail-open fallback installs an unscoped Origin-rewrite rule, re-exposing local Ollama to every website
root_cause: If the self-scoped rule (initiatorDomains:[chrome.runtime.id]) is rejected for any reason, the code falls back to rewriteRule(host, null), which rewrites Origin to http://localhost for ALL initiators reaching the Ollama host. This reintroduces exactly the provider-page exposure the v2.2 audit removed; any web page can then send state-changing requests to the user's local Ollama with a spoofed allowed Origin. The fallback is documented as intentional ('degraded but functional') but is a fail-open security posture.
suggested_fix: Fail closed: if the self-scoped rule cannot be installed, log and leave AI features disabled rather than installing an unscoped rule. Never broaden initiator scope as a fallback.
failure_scenario: A Chrome validation change rejects the extension-id initiator scoping; the fallback installs the unscoped rule. A malicious page POSTs to http://localhost:11434/api/pull or /api/chat with Origin rewritten to the allow-listed http://localhost, triggering model pulls/generation on the user's machine (CSRF-style; reads remain CORS-blocked but writes execute).
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 48 pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection (app.js/DOM or chrome.* API flow not unit-testable without a full harness). Removed the unscoped Origin-rewrite fallback; cors-rules now fails closed (logs, AI 403) instead of widening initiator scope.

title: Every mutation re-reads storage and re-normalises the entire library multiple times
root_cause: A single save/update calls getPrompts() (read + normaliseArray over all prompts and up to 100 versions each), then writeStorage() reads storage AGAIN just to fetch folders (line 163), then writeStore() normalises the whole array a second time (lines 153-159) before writing. This is O(total versions) work twice per mutation and widens the cross-context race window (see #3).
suggested_fix: Read the store once per mutation, carry folders through from that single read, and normalise once; avoid the redundant storageGet in writeStorage and the second normaliseArray in writeStore.
failure_scenario: With a few thousand prompts each holding dozens of versions, every prompt insertion (bumpUseCount) or keystroke-driven save performs two full reads and two full normalisations of the whole store, causing noticeable UI lag and longer read-modify-write windows.
verification_notes: Performance refactor of the core write path: eliminating the double read/normalise requires threading folder state through every mutation (getPrompts returns prompts only) and benchmarking. Beyond minimal scoped edits with regression risk on the storage hot path. transact (#6) already provides a single-read path for sync. Recommend a dedicated, benchmarked follow-up.

Library Suggest now writes categoryId (canonicalCategoryId(newCategory)) when categoryApplied, so the suggestion takes effect in filtering/editor.

title: Translate failure/Stop leaves a partial translation in the textarea with no restore
root_cause: runTranslate streams chunks directly into textarea.value (line 894) but, unlike doImprove (which restores `snapshot` in its catch at line 827), its catch only shows a toast and the finally just re-enables controls. On mid-stream error or user Stop the textarea keeps the truncated translation while stored content is unchanged, and no warning marks the text as partial. failure_scenario: Devices A and B both poll every 30s. B writes edit E to the Dropbox file; Dropbox delivers E to A's folder after A's readSyncFile but before A's writeSyncFile. A overwrites E; on B's next cycle mergeAll takes the remote (pre-E) version because B's local matches its shadow -> E disappears everywhere.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 47 pre-existing warnings, baseline 50). Verified by code inspection (DOM/chrome.*/native flow not unit-testable without a full harness). Both transports re-read the file mtime before writing and skip the write if it changed since read, preventing a cross-device clobber (next cycle merges the fresh remote).

title: Manifest written with ASCII encoding corrupts non-ASCII host paths
root_cause: Set-Content -Encoding ASCII replaces any non-ASCII character in the serialized manifest (which embeds $hostPath derived from the script's directory) with '?'. Windows user profiles with accented/CJK characters are common; the resulting manifest 'path' points at a nonexistent file and Chrome can never launch the host. ExtensionId is also interpolated unvalidated.
suggested_fix: Use -Encoding UTF8 (Chrome accepts UTF-8 manifests; avoid a BOM via [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText with UTF8Encoding($false) on Windows PowerShell 5.1) and validate $ExtensionId against ^[a-p]{32}$.
failure_scenario: User 'C:\Users\José\...' runs install.ps1; the manifest path becomes 'C:\Users\Jos?\...\promptforge-sync-host.bat'. Chrome reports 'Specified native messaging host not found' and native sync cannot be enabled, with no error from the installer.
verification_notes: Verified by code inspection (DOM/chrome.*/native flow not unit-testable without a full harness). install.ps1 writes the manifest as UTF-8 without BOM ([System.IO.File]::WriteAllText + UTF8Encoding($false)) and validates ExtensionId against ^[a-p]{32}$. PowerShell not executed on macOS host.

title: Import/merge toasts report the total library size as the number of imported prompts

Re-importing an unchanged file reports the entire library size as newly imported.

title: Web-accessible resources expose storage modules to all 19 provider origins, and GitHub is matched site-wide
root_cause: promptStorage.js, utils.js, language.js, categories.js are web_accessible to every provider page, letting any script on those sites import extension code (fingerprinting / unnecessary attack surface). The GitHub match is '*://github.com/*' (line 65) while the provider pattern is only '*://github.com/copilot/*', broadening exposure to all of github.com.

verification_notes: REVERTED to keep the manifest loadable. Narrowing WAR matches to provider paths (*://github.com/copilot*) reintroduced the 3.0.0 bug: Chrome rejects path-containing web_accessible_resources.matches (Invalid match pattern → extension fails to load). title: savePrompt upsert path silently resets tags, folderId, language, and groupId when callers omit them
root_cause: On an existing uuid, savePrompt spreads the existing prompt but then overrides with the destructured defaults tags=[], folderId=null, language=null, groupId=null. Unlike updatePrompt (which merges only supplied keys), this wipes those fields. No current caller passes a uuid, so it is latent, but it is a trap in the core storage API right after v3 added language-linked forks.
suggested_fix: In the upsert branch, only override fields the caller actually provided (detect undefined vs defaulted), or document that savePrompt is create-only and route edits through updatePrompt.

verification_notes: npm test → 25/25 pass. tests/promptStorage.test.js: upsert with omitted fields preserves tags/language/groupId. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). savePrompt defaults removed; upsert overrides only provided fields.

title: restoreVersion reads the versions array outside the write lock (TOCTOU)
root_cause: restoreVersion reads prompts and indexes versions[versionIndex] before calling addVersion, which re-reads inside the lock. If another mutation appends a version and triggers the >100 trim between the read and the locked addVersion, the index shifts and a different version's content is restored.
suggested_fix: Perform the version lookup inside the same withLock as the write (read prompts, resolve version, and append atomically), mirroring the rest of the API.
failure_scenario: A prompt at the 100-version cap: user clicks restore of index 5 while a concurrent addVersion appends and trims the oldest entry; indices shift by one and restoreVersion writes the content of what was index 6 instead of the chosen version.
verification_notes: npm test → 25/25 pass. tests/promptStorage.test.js: restoreVersion restores chosen content. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Shared applyVersion helper; restoreVersion resolves+appends inside one withLock (no TOCTOU).

title: suggestTags fallback strips hyphens from tags, contradicting the hyphenated tag convention
root_cause: The fallback character-class removal (line 554) includes '-', so 'code-review' becomes 'codereview' before whitespace is collapsed to hyphens (line 556). The primary JSON path and normalisePrompt keep hyphens, so fallback tags are inconsistent.

verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. suggestTags fallback character class no longer strips '-', so hyphenated tags survive.

title: Context-menu prompt click awaits getPrompts with no try/catch and assumes tab is defined
root_cause: The 'prompt-' branch does `const prompts = await getPrompts()` inside an async listener without a catch; a storage rejection becomes an unhandled rejection. It also dereferences tab.id later without guarding against an undefined tab (some 'all' contexts).
suggested_fix: Wrap the branch in try/catch and guard `if (!tab) return;` before using tab.id.
failure_scenario: chrome.storage.local read fails (quota/serialization) while the user clicks a prompt menu item -> unhandled promise rejection in the service worker, and the click silently does nothing.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. SW prompt-menu branch guards !tab and wraps getPrompts in try/catch.

title: addTagToPrompt returns the whole prompts array on empty tag, but a single prompt otherwise
root_cause: The early return for a blank tag is `return await getPrompts()` (an array), while the normal path returns prompts[idx] (one prompt). Callers expecting a prompt object get an array.
suggested_fix: Return the unchanged prompt (or null) on the empty-tag path to keep the return type consistent.

title: pf-ai 'suggest' op cannot be cancelled; its AbortController is never wired to the call
root_cause: The router creates and stores a controller for every op, but suggestAllMetadata(msg.promptText, msg.language) accepts no signal (ollama-service.js:579), so a {cancel:true} message aborts a controller that controls nothing; the three suggest calls run to their 15s timeouts regardless.

failure_scenario: User triggers auto-suggest then immediately closes the panel/navigates; the cancel message is sent but the suggest requests keep running in the service worker for up to 15s, wasting local Ollama cycles.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. signal threaded through suggestAllMetadata → suggestTitle/Tags/Category → ollamaChat; SW passes its AbortController signal so {cancel:true} aborts.

title: Path-scoped provider patterns require a trailing slash, missing the bare collection URL
root_cause: Patterns '*://github.com/copilot/*' (line 68) and '*://apps.abacus.ai/chatllm/*' (line 131) use path '/copilot/*' which Chrome match-pattern semantics (and the service-worker regex) only match with a trailing slash; the bare https://github.com/copilot URL does not match.

title: Editor load failure leaves a blank editor still bound to the existing prompt uuid
root_cause: If getPrompts() rejects (storage read error), the catch at 642 only toasts; rendering continues with empty fields but promptUuid still set. A subsequent Save runs the update path, overwriting the stored title ('' via null), tags ([]) and content with whatever is in the blank editor.
suggested_fix: On load failure, navigate back to the library (as the not-found branch does) or disable saving until the prompt loads successfully.
failure_scenario: Transient chrome.storage read error while opening #/editor/<uuid>: toast 'Error loading prompt', blank editor. User types a replacement line and hits Save — the original title/tags are wiped and content replaced (original recoverable only via version history).
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. Editor load-failure catch navigates to library instead of leaving a blank editor bound to the uuid.

title: Popup's scheduleBackup never fires — window.close kills the 2s debounce timer
root_cause: After copying, the popup calls scheduleBackup() (autoBackup.js:207-214 uses a 2000ms setTimeout) and then closes the popup after 800ms via setTimeout(() => window.close(), 800). Closing the popup destroys its JS context, cancelling the backup timer; with no app tab open there is no other storage listener to write the backup.
suggested_fix: Await an immediate writeBackup (or send a message to the service worker to perform the backup) before closing, instead of relying on a debounce timer in a dying context.
failure_scenario: Auto-backup enabled, app tab closed. User copies a prompt from the popup; useCount/lastUsedAt are bumped in storage but the backup file is never updated, so the change is missing from the user's cloud-synced restore copy.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. Popup awaits writeBackup(getPrompts()) (completion) before window.close, instead of a 2s debounce timer killed on close.

title: Popup list has the same clear-before-await duplicate-render race as the library
root_cause: loadPrompts clears listEl at line 35 before awaiting getPrompts() at 37 and appends items afterwards. Overlapping calls (200ms search debounce plus a slow storage read/migration) both append their item sets, duplicating entries; there is no stale-render guard.
suggested_fix: Clear the list after the await (right before appending) or use a sequence token to drop stale completions.
failure_scenario: User types in popup search while a legacy migration makes getPrompts slow; two loads overlap and each prompt row appears twice in the popup list.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. Popup loadPrompts uses a loadSeq token to drop stale overlapping renders.

title: Get Started opens a storage-supplied URL without scheme validation

The adjacent pill rendering explicitly validates /^https?:\/\//i (line 114) and the file's own comment treats this map as untrusted, but the Get Started path has no such check (javascript:/data: are blocked by browser/CSP, yet chrome-extension:// or arbitrary https targets pass).

verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. Get Started only renders/opens http(s) URLs (same allowlist as pills).

root_cause: `const text = await file.text()` at line 1777 sits before the try block (1778). A file read rejection (file changed/removed on disk, permission error) escapes doImport as an unhandled rejection with no toast; the read result `text` is also unused since importPrompts re-reads the File.

title: Extension ID interpolated into JSON manifest without validation or escaping
root_cause: $EXT_ID is taken from argv with only a non-empty check and pasted raw into the heredoc JSON (line 33). A value containing a double quote breaks the manifest JSON or injects additional keys (e.g. overriding "path" to an arbitrary executable that Chrome would then launch for that origin); a typo'd ID silently installs a manifest that never matches.
suggested_fix: Validate EXT_ID against ^[a-p]{32}$ before use and reject anything else; optionally JSON-escape $HOST_PATH as well for directories containing quotes/backslashes.
failure_scenario: User pastes an ID with a stray quote or trailing text: the generated manifest is either invalid JSON (host silently never loads) or grants nativeMessaging access to an attacker-chosen binary path.

title: foldConflicts drops tombstones and folders from conflicted copies
root_cause: foldConflicts only folds extra.prompts; extra.tombstones and extra.folders are discarded. A deletion that exists only in a conflicted copy never propagates, and because copies are never deleted and are re-folded every cycle, a copy's prompts can resurrect deleted prompts once the corresponding tombstone is pruned after TOMBSTONE_MAX_AGE_MS (90 days, lines 263-267).
suggested_fix: Also union extra.tombstones (keeping the newest deletedAt per uuid) and merge extra.folders when folding conflicted copies.
failure_scenario: Device B deletes prompt X while offline; Dropbox turns its sync file into a conflicted copy whose tombstones record the deletion. The copy's prompts are folded but its tombstone is dropped; 90+ days later the main file's tombstone for X is pruned and the still-present conflicted copy re-imports X on every cycle.
verification_notes: npm test → 25/25 pass. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. foldConflicts unions tombstones (newest deletedAt per uuid) and folders from conflicted copies.

title: _applyingRemote loop guard released on a fixed 100ms timer
root_cause: The guard that suppresses scheduleSync for remote-caused storage writes is cleared via setTimeout(...,100) (line 341; native: 409). chrome.storage.onChanged delivery is not guaranteed within 100ms (busy tab), and conversely a genuine user edit landing inside the 100ms window is swallowed by scheduleSync's early return (line 463).
suggested_fix: Tag the storage write itself (e.g. compare the incoming change payload against the just-applied merged state, or track a pending-write token) instead of a wall-clock heuristic; at minimum clear the guard on the first observed prompts_storage change rather than after a fixed delay.
failure_scenario: User saves a prompt 50ms after a remote merge applied; scheduleSync sees _applyingRemote=true and skips, so the edit is not pushed to the sync file until the next 30s poll. Under load, the opposite happens: a late onChanged event after 100ms triggers a redundant full sync cycle.
verification_notes: npm test → 25/25 pass. npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. Storage listener clears _applyingRemote on the first prompts_storage change (event-driven); timer reduced to a 3s safety fallback.

title: patchSyncSettings read-modify-write can lose concurrent settings updates
root_cause: patchSyncSettings awaits getSyncSettings then sets {...current, ...patch} with no serialization. Two overlapping patches (sync cycle completion vs UI action) interleave: the later set uses a stale 'current' and drops the earlier patch's fields.
suggested_fix: Serialize patches on a shared promise chain (like promptStorage's withLock) or use a single writer; alternatively store lastSyncAt/lastError under separate storage keys from user-controlled flags.
failure_scenario: User clicks Pause (patchSyncSettings({paused:true})) while runNativeCycle's final patchSyncSettings({lastSyncAt, lastError:null}) is between its get and set. The cycle's set restores paused:false from its stale snapshot — sync keeps running despite the user pausing it.
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). Verified by code inspection. patchSyncSettings serialized on a shared promise chain so overlapping patches can't drop fields.

title: Failed rename leaves orphaned .tmp-<pid> files accumulating in the sync folder
root_cause: The write op writes f + '.tmp-' + process.pid then renameSync; if rename fails (target locked by antivirus on Windows, target is a directory, permissions changed mid-write) the catch returns an error but never unlinks the temp file. Each sync cycle spawns a new host process with a new pid, so every retry litters a new temp file that the cloud provider then syncs to all devices.
suggested_fix: In the catch block, best-effort fs.unlinkSync(tmp) (wrapped in try/catch) before returning the error; optionally reuse a fixed temp name so retries overwrite rather than accumulate.
failure_scenario: promptforge-sync.json is momentarily locked by Windows Defender during renameSync; the write fails, leaving promptforge-sync.json.tmp-1234. The 30s poll retries with pids 1235, 1236, ... filling the Dropbox folder with orphaned temp files synced to every machine.
verification_notes: node --check native-host/promptforge-sync-host.cjs → OK. Verified by code inspection. write op unlinks the temp file in catch (best-effort) so failed renames don't litter .tmp-<pid> files.

title: no-unused-vars ignore patterns miss catch params and destructured arrays — 50 warnings are mostly config noise
root_cause: The rule sets argsIgnorePattern '^_' and varsIgnorePattern '^_' but not caughtErrorsIgnorePattern or destructuredArrayIgnorePattern. ESLint 9 defaults caughtErrors to 'all', so every `catch (_)` and `const [_, x]` placeholder is flagged despite the documented '^_' convention (CLAUDE.md). npm run lint reports 50 warnings, 0 errors; the majority are these intentional placeholders, which trains reviewers to ignore lint output.
suggested_fix: Add caughtErrorsIgnorePattern: '^_' and destructuredArrayIgnorePattern: '^_' to the no-unused-vars options so the config matches the documented convention; then triage the remaining genuine warnings (unused 'dirty' at app.js:646 is finding #2, unused IMPORT_SUCCESS_RESET_MS at content.js:141, etc.).
failure_scenario: Developer runs npm run lint, sees 50 warnings that are all intentional '_' placeholders, and dismisses the output — missing the genuinely dead 'dirty' flag that signals the unsaved-changes data-loss bug (#2).
verification_notes: npm run lint → exit 0 (0 errors; 28 genuine pre-existing warnings). no-unused-vars now sets caughtErrorsIgnorePattern + destructuredArrayIgnorePattern '^_'; warning count dropped 47 → 28 (remaining are genuine unused vars).
